page: Microsoft Azure DC4ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine deployed on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory allocation stands at 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per vCPU). The CPU features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic extensions. Unlike base compute instances, this configuration includes a bundled 161 GB local SSD for high-speed scratch storage, alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are absent.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent single-thread execution alongside constrained multi-core throughput due to the 2-core hardware boundary. In Geekbench testing, the instance recorded a single-core score of 1219.0 (mid-tier performance) and a multi-core score of 2686.0 (lower tier). Similarly, stress-ng benchmarks reflect an average single-core rating of 2185.16, contrasted with a lower-quartile multi-core rating of 4242.25. The PassMark CPU evaluation reached 4724.98, while memory testing produced a score of 1701.64. Redis throughput reached 3.06 million SET operations per second, ranking in the lower quartile among comparable enterprise instances.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the DC4ads_v5 offers an integrated compute-plus-storage profile where local SSD capacity removes the immediate need to provision external temporary disks. However, users seeking dense parallel compute will face scalability bottlenecks given the two physical core limitation. The instance is best suited for general-purpose enterprise tasks, internal microservices, moderate web serving, CI/CD runners, and development workloads requiring moderate memory with fast local scratch space.
description: Microsoft Azure DC4ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor using the x86_64 architecture. Managed under Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 4 dedicated vCPUs spread across 2 physical cores, paired with 16.0 GB of memory and a bundled 161 GB local SSD. It includes no hardware GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show balanced single-core execution, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1219.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 2185.16, while multi-core metrics remain constrained by the low core count. PassMark CPU reached 4724.98 and Redis achieved 3.06 million SET operations per second. By providing dedicated compute, integrated fast scratch disk, and a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the DC4ads_v5 serves general-purpose web tiers, CI/CD workers, and lightweight database environments.
